title: Fraction coefficients under isomorphisms of quotient lines
statement: Let $h:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal E$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], $L$ invertible [def-sc-invertible-module], $q:h^*\mathcal E\to L$ an epimorphism, and $\psi$ a graded extension [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map]. For an isomorphism $v:L\xrightarrow{\sim}L'$, a quotient $q'=q;v$, and any graded extension $\psi'$ of $q'$, all degree-$d$ scalar coefficients of $\psi$ and $\psi'$ coincide in the corresponding frames $l$ and $v(l)$, on every affine $W$ over an affine $U$ and for every homogeneous $c\in\operatorname{Sym}^d(\mathcal E(U))$. Every morphism $F$ satisfying $\mathrm{HasQuotientFractionCharts}$ for $(\psi,q)$ satisfies the same predicate for $(\psi',q')$. The coefficient functions and chart predicate are those of [lem-trf-line-quotient-homogeneous-fraction-map].

source.place: Tags 01OA (section-projective-bundle) and 01O4 (lemma-apply-relative); inverse quotient constructions and their arbitrary-pullback compatibility, with the explicit degree-one chart calculations.

proof.text: The degree-one extension equations and quotient compatibility identify the components after the tensor power of v. Induct on the right-generated powers of the degree-one symmetric submodule: structural scalars use the unit, sums use additivity, and products use the tensor-power addition comparison. Tensor powers of v carry the frame l to the frame v(l); both frame scalar maps are injective, so all homogeneous coefficients agree. The same argument in degree one identifies the generator coefficients. On each affine W every frame of the target is the image of a unique source frame. Transport the seven conjuncts of HasQuotientFractionCharts along these equalities, using linearity of v for frame changes and naturality of v for restrictions. The localization domains, fraction values, scalar maps, scheme equations and overlap units coincide. This proves chart compatibility without appealing to the fraction-map existence or uniqueness theorem.

lean.statement: theorem lineQuotient_iso_charts {S T : Scheme.{u}} (h : T ⟶ S) (E : S.Modules) [E.IsQuasicoherent] (L : T.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (q : (tensorPullback h).obj E ⟶ L) [Epi q] (ψ : RelativeGradedLineMap h (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E) L) (hψ : ψ.ExtendsLineQuotient h E L q) (L' : T.Modules) (v : L ≅ L') (q' : (tensorPullback h).obj E ⟶ L') (hq : q ≫ v.hom = q') (ψ' : RelativeGradedLineMap h (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E) L') (hψ' : ψ'.ExtendsLineQuotient h E L' q') : (∀ (U : S.affineOpens) (W : T.affineOpens) (hWU : W.1 ≤ h ⁻¹ᵁ U.1) (l : Γ(L, W.1)), IsFreeGenerator l → ∀ (d : ℕ) (c : (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).grading U d), ψ'.quotientCoefficient U W hWU (v.hom.app W.1 l) d c = ψ.quotientCoefficient U W hWU l d c) ∧ ∀ F : T ⟶ (SymmetricAlgebraSheaf.gradedAlgebraData E).relProj, ψ.HasQuotientFractionCharts h E L q F → ψ'.HasQuotientFractionCharts h E L' q' F
